scope: Explicit author outlooks and narrowly closed follow-up tests for quantum backflow; source extraction only, no simulations in this branch.

sources.title: General quantum backflow in realistic wave packets
sources.short_quote: uses a smoothed spatial window rather than a sharp one
explicit_author_outlooks: Determine how general backflow changes when the spatial probability measurement is smoothed.
Ensure experimental violations do not originate from failure of dynamical assumptions such as force-free motion.
Understand the relation between the standard and generalized dimensionless backflow constants.
Explore general backflow and reentry beyond free-particle evolution when motion direction is preserved.
sources.important_completed_work_not_a_gap: The paper already derives general backflow for arbitrary momentum distributions, works out two-Gaussian examples, and proves backflow/overflow mutual incompatibility. Standard positive-momentum smoothing is acknowledged as known prior work.
sources.local_adaptation_status: Applying the question to cosine-lattice velocities and finite detector windows is our proposed adaptation, not a result in this continuum paper. Its numerical continuum constants must not be transplanted.

sources.title: Quantum backflow in biased tight-binding systems
locations: Section VII Conclusions and outlook, PDF pp.20-21; especially final paragraph p.21
explicit_author_outlooks: Extend the analysis to SSH models, arrival-time distributions, Bloch packets in periodic potentials, disordered systems, and quantum walks.
Construct packets from nonnegative-momentum eigenstates in these systems; the authors identify this prerequisite as challenging.
Use stronger discrete backflow to broaden possible experimental detection approaches.
sources.important_completed_work_not_a_gap: The paper already solves instantaneous and time-integrated backflow optimization in biased/unbiased infinite and periodic nearest-neighbor chains.
sources.local_adaptation_status: Finite-resolution preparation-aware optimization or a controlled two-band SSH example are proposed tests; neither is an author-reported result in this source.

sources.title: Preparing Quantum Backflow States by Large Momentum Transfer
locations: Conclusion, PDF p.9; source text lines939-979
sources.short_quote: stronger backflow is accompanied by a shorter density-modulation length scale
explicit_author_outlooks: Adapt LMT-based atom-interferometric preparation to the general-backflow framework for realistic wave packets.
Investigate fluorescence or absorption density measurements at multiple evolution times as a route to the generalized position-measurement witness.
sources.important_completed_work_not_a_gap: The paper already proposes the LMT protocol, analyzes adjustable arm amplitudes/momentum separation and a critical-density signature, and identifies the stronger-current versus finer-fringe tradeoff. It is a preparation/theory proposal, not a completed matter-wave backflow observation.
sources.local_adaptation_status: A cosine-lattice PSF/witness test transfers the detection question; it does not reproduce the cold-atom LMT protocol or its dimensional parameters.

candidates.title: Detector-resolved general backflow under simple state preparation
candidates.priority_reason: Explicit author follow-up with a directly measurable witness and a small, falsifiable local test.
candidates.source_gap: Paterek-Goussev Discussion p.4 explicitly leaves smoothed-window general backflow open; Chen-Tang v2 Conclusion p.9 proposes linking LMT preparation to generalized multitime density measurements and highlights the fine-fringe detection tradeoff.
candidates.observation: Existing pi/2 Gaussian gives a sharp-cut event only about 3.35e-5 of probability, potentially lost by finite resolution.
candidates.hypothesis: Optimizing the experimentally resolved probability witness, instead of sharp-cut current or peak backflow, can trade ideal magnitude for robustness to detector width.
candidates.model: Homogeneous one-dimensional cosine band; no force, loss, disorder or nonlinear interaction. Use present exact FFT solver.
state_families: Strict positive-velocity projection as a control
A normalized two-Gaussian coherent superposition with unrestricted velocity signs; separately record negative-velocity weight
candidates.witness: Delta_w = sum_n W_w(n-b)[P_n(t2)-P_n(t1)] - P(v<0), with W_w monotone decreasing and 0<=W_w<=1; w=0 is a sharp cut.
candidates.classical_bound: For any classical ensemble with conserved velocity sign, a monotone bounded left-window can increase by at most the initial negative-velocity probability. Thus Delta_w<=0 remains the null.
candidates.minimal_parameters: Initial sigma=4 or6 sites; detector widths w/a=0,0.25,0.5,1,2,4; one fixed event from existing trace plus a bounded two-Gaussian search. Freeze selected state before comparing held-out widths and small parameter perturbations.
baselines: Same normalized state with sharp detector
Same state and time window with each smoothed detector
State optimized for sharp witness versus state optimized for a chosen finite detector width
Incoherent mixture of the two packets to remove cross interference
closed_checks: Direct probability difference equals time-integrated weighted current
N doubling and fixed-cut boundary-flux check
Negative-velocity weight included rather than ignored
Report normalization, initial spatial RMS width, preparation complexity and detector width for every comparison

For an explicit independent-position-sampling model, estimate shot requirements from the variance of the fixed detector response; do not claim the same noise model for classical optical intensity detection.
candidates.falsifier: If no positive resolved witness survives the chosen finite resolution and preparation budget, this route fails for that domain; a larger sharp-cut value alone is not success.
candidates.demo: Show the two measured density snapshots, the detector response window, the sharp and resolved witnesses, and an incoherent-control trace.
candidates.novelty_boundary: Standard positive-spectrum smoothing is known. A lattice Gaussian subtest is only a detector-feasibility demonstration; a full general-backflow tradeoff and prior-art comparison would still be needed.

candidates.title: Construct and test a positive-group-velocity SSH packet
candidates.priority_reason: The tight-binding paper explicitly names SSH and the positive-sector construction prerequisite.
candidates.source_gap: Torres Arvizu et al. Section VII p.21.
candidates.hypothesis: A band-resolved spectral projector gives a controlled positive-velocity state, permitting an unambiguous fixed-cut backflow test in the SSH chain.
candidates.model: Two-site unit-cell SSH Hamiltonian with real intracell/intercell hopping; compare uniform chain t1=t2 with dimerized t1/t2 ratios and keep bandwidth or maximum speed normalization explicit.
candidates.minimal_parameters: Ncell=128 then256; ratios t1/t2=0.7,1,1/0.7; one Gaussian spectral width and one fixed finite time window. Use full Bloch spinors and numerical group-velocity sign projectors.
baselines: Incoherent band mixture if an interband superposition is tested
Swap unit-cell definition and physical cut consistently
closed_checks: Direct site continuity holds for both bond types
Fixed-cut integrated current agrees with probability change
N doubling and gap/velocity normalization checks
candidates.falsifier: If any negative transfer disappears after a proper velocity projection or comes from boundary reflection, it is not the intended free-propagation backflow.
candidates.demo: Plot band/velocity selection, two-sublattice packet evolution and the measured cut flux.
candidates.novelty_boundary: This first test would validate a construction, not establish topological enhancement. Exchanging t1 and t2 changes the unit-cell/cut relation; bulk backflow differences cannot be called topological without additional invariant controls.

not_selected_for_minimal_demo.question: Exact relation between generalized and standard backflow constants
not_selected_for_minimal_demo.reason: Explicit fundamental outlook, but numerical toy examples would not resolve the analytic relation; poor fit for a short closed demo.

not_selected_for_minimal_demo.question: Disorder robustness interpreted as strict free backflow
not_selected_for_minimal_demo.reason: Disorder changes velocity sign and causes ordinary reflection; the witness must first be reformulated. A bare disorder simulation risks a false positive.

time_sensitive_caution: A July2026 entangled-photon transverse-momentum backflow report exists (2607.10281v1). Do not repeat March2026 wording that backflow has never been observed without distinguishing optical/transverse analogs from the longitudinal matter-wave probability dynamics at issue.
